concepts.def: Rigid bar pivoting at a fulcrum; classified into three classes by arrangement.
Toothed wheel meshing with another; transmits motion and changes torque/speed.
Wheel with grooved rim and a rope or belt; can change direction and reduce effort.
Rotating cam pushes a follower up/down, converting rotary to reciprocating motion.
Series of pivoted bars producing different motion outputs; e.g., parallel motion.
Output force / input force; ratio measuring how a mechanism multiplies effort.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Mechanisms — a core area of GCSE Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Mechanisms brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Mechanisms.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
